title: Diffusion-guided design tests bimetallic ammonia-decomposition catalysts
summary: A diffusion model guided by a learned nitrogen-adsorption predictor generated bimetallic candidates near the target adsorption energy. Co75Mo25 was among the generated candidates and maps exactly to the tested Co3Mo1 ratio; under the reported supported-catalyst assay it reached 18.6 μmol gmetal⁻¹ s⁻¹ at 520 °C, about twice the paper’s Ru reference under its stated test. Co–Mo catalysts are established prior art, so this entry does not claim the first Co–Mo ammonia-decomposition catalyst or global composition novelty. Ex-situ XRD showed oxidized phases after air exposure and does not establish the working active phase.
ai_technology: Diffusion model guided by random-forest nitrogen-adsorption predictor
organization: Worcester Polytechnic Institute; University of California, Riverside; University of Massachusetts Lowell

evidence.tested: Authors report Co3Mo1 catalyst performance under a defined gas-flow, temperature, support, loading and pretreatment protocol; Co75Mo25 is the corresponding generated candidate.
evidence.unknown: Exact composition/formulation prior art, long-term stability, energy efficiency and scale-up remain unresolved; this draft makes no global-priority claim.
evidence.ai_role: A random-forest adsorption-energy predictor guides diffusion denoising; DFT and laboratory testing evaluate generated candidates.

source_review.scope: Primary PMC full text opened; article metadata and candidate/experimental mapping reconciled using continuation audit dated 2026-11-16.
